don ' t know why you ' re being downvoted for stating the truth . by italian law , moscato d’asti can only be 5 . 5 % abv . this is why it ' s so sweet - the fermentation process is halted before most of the natural sugar can be converted into alcohol . of course , domestic stuff can be higher , but most is still around 5 % - 7 % abv to retain its sweetness . drinking a whole bottle of even a relatively high abv moscoto is roughly the equivalent of drinking three 5 % abv beers . depending on your body weight and tolerance that might fuck you up , but most people would not be drunk .

i ' ll start with a few of my favorites from the last decade : 1 . [ shaun of the dead : it ' s not the end of the world ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = l93fdmh6xko ) . edgar wright and simon pegg have incorporated awesome drinking scenes into all of their movies ( and their [ next film ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = n _ _ 1y - n5tqk ) involves an epic pub crawl while the world is ending ) , but this is probably my favorite . if you drunks are anything like me , you ' ve been in this situation before , trying to cheer up your friend with dick jokes and flaming sambuca , singing ' 80s hip hop anthems in the street , and capping the night off by waking up your prick roommate with electro . 2 . [ the sopranos : christopher moltisanti gets belligerent ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = 4glw5icenik ) . the drug and alcohol scenes in the sopranos are incredibly realistic . in this one , christopher breaks his aa code and gets liquored up with paulie , whom he recently fought with . i ' ve definitely been here before , getting so intoxicated that some mild ball - busting comes across as fighting words , going on tangents and forgetting the point you were trying to make , and having your friend nod along concernedly as if he understands what the fuck you ' re talking about . the looks that chris ' friends and family give him are all too familiar , inferring that you are " that guy " tonight . 3 . [ beerfest : drinking games ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = hulzkclvsz4 ) . much of the world laughs at north americans for their drinking games , claiming that anyone who needs games to get drunk is a pussy , but i grew up with them and still love them . this scene showcases a few classics , including shotgunning , viking , never have i ever , and strikeout . it ' s a silly , low - brow movie , which is often exactly what i ' m looking for . 4 . [ the outdoorsmen : 4 beer chug ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = uhijcnkocmm ) . getting indie here . the outdoorsmen is a 2005 documentary about a bunch of washingtonian buddies who go into the woods , form teams of 2 , and compete in 15 events , all of which involve speed drinking . the reason i enjoy this scene in particular is that it ' s the first event of the day , when everyone is still feeling cocky , bright - eyed , and bushy - tailed , plus we get to see a dude hose . seek this movie out . 5 . [ team america : world police : dicks , pussies , and assholes ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = xetgu _ unr08 ) . sometimes , drunks can be profound . this scene is hysterical and disturbingly familiar . if you ' ve hung around as many pubs as i have , you ' ve probably waxed philosophical with an elderly , scraggly bearded gentleman . if you ' ve drank as much as i have , you ' ve probably vomited uncontrollably in an alleyway , too . 6 . [ sideways : spit bucket ] ( http : / / makemomentum . files . wordpress . com / 2012 / 10 / sideways - spit - bucket . jpg ) . couldn ' t find the clip , but if you can , it ' s amazing . miles , a struggling writer , just received word that his book won ' t be published . he ' s also suffered a terrible divorce and recently found out his ex is getting remarried . needless to say , he needs a drink , and when the host won ' t give him more than a tasting size , he chugs the spit bucket . there ' s very little more degrading to a drunk than being cut off at a bar , especially when you ' re still in control , and paul giamatti exemplifies that frustration . i can only hope to one day match his tenacity . also , this movie is incredibly adept at making me feel like i ' ve been drinking wine all day : dizzying highs , giggle fits , and melancholy all in one . 7 . [ superbad : saturday was actually a crazy night for me ] ( http : / / www . youtube . com / watch ? v = za9fc5g1vz0 ) . another movie with many classic drinking scenes , but this hits closest to home . college certainly helped me come out of my shell , but before that , my high school partying consisted of me and my friends getting loaded in someone ' s basement , watching porn , funnelling beers , vomiting on each other , drunkenly encountering our friends ' parents , chugging hot sauce , and unsuccessfully trying to get into shitty clubs . and yet when girls i liked would ask what i had gotten up to on the weekend , i sold our pathetic romps as the greatest parties ever . strangely , this scene is incredibly nostalgic for me .

addiction is a thing . self destructive behaviour is a thing . alcohol is a way for both of those things to happen . addiction can happen when you drink because it used to bring you relief , now it doesn ' t but you still drink anyways . or when you drink in anticipation of stress . keep in mind the literally close to half the world is addicted to caffeine . if they took it out of their diet they ' d have withdrawal . quite frankly you ' re too young to get addicted to alcohol but you could be developing addictive tendencies . it ' s also genetic , which means you can be both prone and resistant to it by default . drinking the night before an exam is poor self control . drinking in the bathroom between classes and being edgy if you don ' t is a problem . some people are self abusive / have other psychiatric issues . go to iraq and see a kid blown apart , you might use alcohol to fix it . the person isn ' t addicted to it per se , they are just using it for the wrong reasons . however untreated it could turn into an addiction . i was in italy for a month . people drank wine for breakfast , lunch , and dinner . alcoholism is a thing here the same reason people think work is some natural , just thing , puritanism . that , combined with the forbidden fruit issue with a 21 year old drinking age , one of three in the world ( a lot of countries just ban it ) , makes for a whole lot of repressed issues .

no it isn ' t , it ' s your body preventing alcohol poisoning when you puke when you ' re drunk . when you get a hangover that is because your body is dehydrated ( cause of many symptoms including swollen blood vessels in the brain resulting in headaches and dizziness ) , drained of electrolytes and you ' ve converted the alcohol into acetaldehyde which is a poison , your body slowly processes it expending an enormous amount of energy which compounds the problem making you tired . that is completely different to alcohol poisoning , mild alcohol poisoning might make your hangover worse but it isn ' t the sole cause of hangovers . come back when you ' ve grown some pubes kid , in my day we ' d just put this guy on his front in the shed and let him sober up - no one had any issue with it they just walked in at 6am looking sheepish as hell and cleaned themselves up , serious alcohol poisoning is more of a case of " holy shit his heart is beating really slowly and he ' s turning blue " at which point you phone the ambulance , but to achieve that level of drunkeness at which your body won ' t reject enough alcohol through vomiting , that takes some doing . i ' ve only ever seen one instance and the guy was drinking like a motherfucker after having thrown up the first time .

& gt ; _ _ alcohol flush reaction _ _ is a condition in which an individual develops flushes or blotches associated with [ erythema ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / erythema ) on the face , neck , shoulders , and , in some cases , the entire body after consuming [ alcoholic beverages ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / ethanol ) . the reaction is the result of an accumulation of [ acetaldehyde ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / acetaldehyde ) , a metabolic byproduct of the [ catabolic ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / catabolic ) metabolism of alcohol , and is caused by an [ aldehyde dehydrogenase ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / aldehyde _ dehydrogenase ) deficiency . & gt ; this syndrome has been associated with an increased risk of [ esophageal cancer ] ( https : / / en . wikipedia . org / wiki / esophageal _ cancer ) in those who drink . it has also been associated with lower than average rates of alcoholism , possibly due to its association with adverse effects after drinking alcohol . & gt ; because of the association with asian ancestry , alcohol flush reaction has also been referred to by such informal names as _ _ asian flush syndrome _ _ , _ _ asian flush _ _ , and _ _ asian glow _ _ . & gt ; alcohol has paradoxical effects . which is quite common in fact , a number of substances and a number of disorders have effects or symptoms that seem utterly contradictory . for example , depression can cause excessive physical motion , or an absence of physical motion . it can cause excessive sleep or sleeplessness . alcohol can cause raucous behavior , it can also put you to bed . the way to understand it that makes most sense to me is that alcohol can suppress social anxiety , which is one of its first effects . it can also suppress other things , ultimately suppressing your basic bodily functions if you drink too much . i haven ' t seen much of a direct link between alcohol and depression , but there are some complex interactions . having a drink with friends can help depression , getting hammered alone can definitely compound depression . being addicted certainly doesn ' t help either . anyway , being a depressant means that it pushes certain aspects of your psychology and behavior down . that isn ' t always a bad thing , and excitation of certain behaviors can also be good and bad . the upper / downer distinction is more about how it acts neurologically . and since humans have competing neurological systems ( the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems at the more general level ) , either one can have positive or negative effects , depending on the situation , particular effects , and usage levels .

i mostly agree with your conclusion but there is plenty of evidence that drinking alcohol leads to dehydration . alcohol essentially prevents your kidneys from retaining water , and on average you ' ll pee out a few extra beers ' worth of fluid when you drink . sweating , vomiting , and diarrhea ( all more common when drunk ) can also contribute . basically dehydration does happen , even with beer , and drinking water definitely helps fix dehydration . the link between dehydration and hangover is less defined , but drinking water is certainly more likely to help than to hurt .

that ' s not quite right , i think you ' ve confused a few things there . pure ethanol is no more poisonous than the ethanol in a bottle of vodka ( both are , of course , technically toxins , that ' s why you get fucked up . ) what you might be thinking of is methanol , which is often a byproduct of distillation , and if you don ' t properly separate it from the ethanol , can cause you to go blind / die . it ' s why hillbilly moonshine is bad for you . as for the whole & gt ; 95 . 5 % thing , that ' s just because ethanol has a polar part to its molecule that really loves water , if you had 100 % ethanol , you would either have to keep it sealed up , or it would pull water out of the air until it reduced to ~ 95 . 5 % .

there are a number of comforts in being drunk , and not all indicate a problem . it is really easy to not be self conscious when drunk . it is really easy to have a good time when drunk . it is really easy to be confident when drunk . none of these are bad things . but if you find that you can ' t have a good time without alcohol , or you find that you can ' t get through the day or the week without alcohol , that is an issue . the ultimate test is whether your drinking causes problems in other parts of your life . if you hurt the people you care about because of your drinking , or you hurt yourself , or you neglect the things that are important to you , then it is a problem . but the reason we drink is that it is nice , drinking has a cost and it has a benefit . i ' m going to feel pretty shitty tomorrow , i ' m going to have to work out to burn the calories i consumed tonight , but i ' m also having a good time . if your drinking is a problem , you can ' t balance the positives and negatives , if your drinking is not a problem , you can ( within a reasonable margin of error ) , hit the sweet spot where you get the pleasantness of intoxication , but don ' t incur excessive hangovers , long term health problems , or destruction of relationships . being drunk is nice , and recognizing that is fine . it is only when that nice feeling comes at the expense of things more important that you have a problem .

bac is what determines how drunk you feel . the factors affecting changes in bac are rate of consumption , stomach contents ( affects how quickly the stomach drains into the intestine ) alcohol concentration ( the concentration difference between your blood and what ' s in your intestines determines how quickly it will flux into your blood , so straight whiskey on an empty stomach will get you feeling it fast ) and the saturation level of the enzymes in your liver ( determines how quickly alcohol is removed from the blood ) . the rate of blood flow or partial pressure of oxygen are not , to my knowledge , significant factors . drinking when you ' re new to high altitudes will make you feel drunker because it exacerbates altitude sickness . i moved to denver awhile back and noticed this my first weekend here , but have since regained the tolerance i had in az .
